title: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte
votes_base: two-thirds of the senator-judges able to take part (20 of 24 now), rounded up

articles.t: Misuse of confidential funds (Office of the Vice President and DepEd)
Unexplained wealth, incomplete SALNs (2022–2025) and prohibited business interests
Alleged threats against the President, the First Lady and a former Speaker

claims: A forensic financial analyst for the prosecution estimated about ₱817 million in unexplained assets. The defense disputes the figure.
Prosecutors say the case rests mainly on documents: her SALNs, corporate financial statements, tax and property records, firearms registrations and financial transaction reports.
The Vice President denies wrongdoing and calls the proceedings political harassment.

timeline.t: First impeachment: 215 House members sign the complaint and send it to the Senate.
Supreme Court voids the first impeachment under the one-year bar. No trial is held.
Senate votes 19–4 (1 present) to archive the first articles.
Second impeachment: 257 House members vote to impeach and send four articles to the Senate.
Senate trial begins. Sen. Chiz Escudero is elected presiding officer and sets 16 votes to convict.
Day 29: court votes 13–1 to count only senator-judges able to take part. Votes needed fall to 14.
Prosecution drops Articles I, III and IV (Day 39). Only Article II, unexplained wealth, remains.
Prosecution rests its case after nearly four months of testimony.
Defense starts its evidence (Day 40). First witness: Davao City Assessor's Office officer Jaime Adalin. The court served 22 of 24 subpoenas the defense asked for.
Defense witnesses: Samal City assessor John Kenneth Enumerables and Davao City accountant Vingelin Bajan.

GenCorp corporate counsel Suzette Balucanag-Punay testifies for the defense that GenCorp paid the Vice President ₱2,142,369.14 as return of capital in 2022–2025 and that the Vice President held no GenCorp shares or posts in those years. Senator-judges press her on why the SALNs list GenCorp shares.

next.t: Full day. Defense to present BPI senior vice president Atty. Paul Roderick Ysmael.
